headline: Took Madison Design Build's site health from 82 to 90
why: His SEO/AEO report and Webflow audit landed 10/20, and he set up AI prompt tracking in SE Ranking on his own initiative. Adam routed it straight to Peyton.
say: The Madison Design Build report was sharp. Getting site health from 82 to 90 and setting up AI prompt tracking without being asked is exactly the ownership I want on every client.

headline: Closed out the Stanwood Camano Troll launch completely
why: Search Console, analytics, sitemap and header photo, with the launch checklist closed 10/21 at 5:04 pm and handed to Adam. Nothing left dangling.
say: Stanwood Camano was a clean finish. Every launch item done and handed off the same day. That's the standard.

headline: Absorbed Josh's last-minute GMU deck without dropping the ball
why: On 10/21 she put her own SafeTraces work aside to cover an urgent deck for Josh, then picked SafeTraces straight back up 10/22.
say: Thanks for jumping on the GMU deck for Josh. I saw it cost you your SafeTraces time, and I appreciate you flexing for the team. Let me know if that keeps happening so I can protect your plan.

headline: Got the JMU bulldog graphic to two strong options
why: Two revision rounds on the schedule graphic, then options A and B to Adam on 10/21. She also shipped the Western Rugby Alumni season program to print.
say: The JMU options are great. Giving Adam an A and a B instead of one take made it an easy decision. And nice work getting the Western program out the door.

headline: Got the Western pre-order banner live in 38 minutes
why: Josh handed him the banner on 10/22 at 11:51 am, already a day past due. David had it live on wwurugby.org by 12:29 pm, right after standup, and passed it to Peyton with days to spare before the 10/25 pre-order cutoff.
say: Saw you turned the Western pre-order banner around in under 40 minutes yesterday, even though it showed up already late. That's what lets the strategists say yes to clients. Thanks, man.

headline: Took the JMU alumni update page live the same evening
why: On 10/21 between 6:26 and 7:25 pm he built /update-your-information, flagged that Bloomerang's embed came in unstyled, and went through five rounds of fixes with Josh (new embed file, button, nav label). He pushed it live before signing off.
say: The JMU update-your-information page was a messy one with the Bloomerang embed, and you stuck with Josh through every round that evening until it was live. I appreciate you not leaving it half-done overnight.

headline: Reviewed the Olson site brand before being asked
why: At standup 10/22 she'd already looked over the new Olson site on her own and narrowed the open issues to the logo and colors. She also caught that five different Olson logos are in use and planned the 12/2 board deck for 10/28, ahead of her days off.
say: Thanks for looking over the Olson site before I'd even asked. Getting it down to just the logo and colors, and catching the five-logo mess, makes the launch much easier for me.

headline: Saw the Meyer Art Center cleanup through to the end
why: He closed the last round of the Meyer Art Center refinement list (nav timing, hovers, scroll animations, sticky spacing) on 10/22 and sent it to Adam, then sat through another hour of edits with Adam and Peyton. At standup 10/23 he said it felt good to finally finish.
say: Meyer Art Center has been a long one, and you kept working the refinement list until it was actually closed, then took another hour of edits with Adam and Peyton without complaint. That kind of follow-through is why clients trust our launches.

headline: Turned Adam's same-day JMU and Troll list around by evening
why: Adam assigned a six-item request across jmurugby.com and stanwoodcamanotroll.com (FAQs into a CMS collection, supporter logo order, latest-3 news, a new troll FAQ) at 1:05 pm on Friday 10/23, due that day. David had it updated and back to Adam by 5:37 pm, and Adam closed it over the weekend with no follow-ups.
say: Adam dropped that six-item JMU and Troll list on you Friday afternoon and you had it back to him before the end of the day, clean enough that he just closed it. Thanks for making a same-day ask feel easy.

headline: Added usage guidelines to the JMU logo presentation
why: On 10/23 at 5:23 pm she handed Adam the start of Josh's JMU logo presentation: both logo options, each shown beside the JMU Club Rugby mark, and first guidelines for using them alone and together. She went past showing logos into how the brand should be used.
say: I liked that the JMU logo deck didn't stop at two options. Showing them beside the club mark and writing first guidelines for how they work together is real brand work, and it's exactly the direction I want us heading.

headline: Kept five decks on brand while AI kept breaking them
why: At standup 10/23 she was carrying five decks with two more coming from Peyton, alongside SafeTraces and USA Youth. She's checking every page of the Claude-generated decks because fonts and colors come back changed, and she called her load manageable by prioritizing.
say: I know the deck load is heavy right now, and you're still checking every page so the fonts and colors hold up when the AI versions come back broken. That care doesn't go unnoticed. Tell me when the stack gets to be too much and I'll help move things.

headline: Finished the ECA design comments two days early
why: At standup 10/26 Blair asked for the ECA design feedback to be worked through by Wednesday 10/28. David closed the Design Review at 5:44 pm that same day and passed the design to Peyton at 5:48 pm, while also closing Ride the Tide Development and starting on the roughly 15 tasks Adam sent over the weekend.
say: I asked for ECA by Wednesday and you had it back to Peyton Monday evening, with a full weekend list from Adam on top. That gets the client moving and clears the way for the chatbot and dashboard work coming next. Nice work.

headline: Gave the client portal its first real product call
why: When Blair demoed the client portal at standup 10/26 and asked for first reactions, David was the one with a concrete note: tone down the page-to-page animation because it's a utility product and clients shouldn't feel overloaded. Blair took it on as a follow-up the same morning.
say: Your call on the portal animation was right. It's a tool people come to get something done, and that kind of product thinking is exactly what I want from you as we build more of these. Keep pushing back on my stuff like that.

headline: Brought a ready-made handoff plan for her time off
why: At standup 10/26, when Blair asked how coverage worked before, Jamie offered the system she and Chris used: a task listing every link and what's needed, tagging Adam and each project's strategist. She also set every deliverable (Olson, Adam's Thursday deck, Meyer posters and mailers, two Crusaders decks) to land by Wednesday before she's out 10/29–10/30, and took on the Crusaders content herself after Josh and Adam couldn't get to it.
say: Thanks for walking in with an answer when I asked about coverage. The handoff task with links and the strategists tagged is exactly what I need, since I'm not close to your day-to-day. Let's make it how we handle anyone being out.
